title: Make the dev-case promote path trustworthy
brief: Reviewers say the auto-advance behavior around evaluated dev-case submissions feels inconsistent and hard to trust — sometimes the system's advice doesn't match what it actually does. Make the promote path trustworthy. You decide what that means, what to fix first, and how far to go within the timebox.
repoSeed: The kp repository itself. Start from the promote flow: app/_lib/devcase-orchestrator.ts (the ranked stage), app/_lib/devcase-run.ts (promoteSubmission), app/_lib/dev-control.ts (the calibration floor), and app/api/devcase/promote/route.ts (the manual promote path).
tasks: Trace end-to-end how an evaluated submission advances (or is held): the orchestrator's ranked stage, promoteSubmission, the calibration floor, and the manual promote route. Identify where behavior and advice diverge.
Fix the divergence(s) you judge matter most within the timebox.
Show how you verified your change works — including that the other callers of what you touched still behave.
Keep a short DECISIONS log: for every call you made where the brief was open — what you chose, the alternative you rejected, and why.

coverProbes.where: the brief's 'trustworthy' — behavioral consistency vs stricter evidence gating vs reviewer-facing transparency
coverProbes.reveals: Do they name the possible readings, pick one deliberately and scope it — or build whatever the model suggests first?
decisionSpace: Align the advice with the calibrated floor so what the system says matches what it does
Gate harder on evidence quality (confidence/authenticity) so weak evidence never auto-advances
Change no behavior; surface the reasons (floor, scores, confidence) to reviewers so decisions are explainable

coverProbes.where: the promote flow's existing contracts — idempotent promotion, the audit trail, the human-gated adverse-action rule, and two callers of promoteSubmission
coverProbes.reveals: Do they read the surrounding freeze/dedup/audit contracts before changing the flow, or generate over them?
decisionSpace: Work within the existing contracts and keep changes local to the advice/gate computation
Extend the contract deliberately (e.g. thread the floor through) and update both callers
Rework the promote flow and accept the re-verification burden

coverProbes.where: a fix that looks right in the orchestrator but silently changes the manual promote route's behavior, or breaks the existing unit tests around promotion — passes a quick read
coverProbes.reveals: Do they check the second caller and run the tests, or trust a one-file read?
decisionSpace: Run the unit suite and grep for every caller before shipping
Manually trace both call paths and document the trace
Rely on the one file compiling and ship

midFlightUpdate.update: Update from the team: compliance just flagged that any automated advance/hold decision must be explainable to the candidate on request. Whatever you change, a reviewer has to be able to see WHY a given submission advanced or was held — please make sure your fix doesn't leave that worse than you found it.
midFlightUpdate.reveals: Do they reconcile explainability with their chosen fix (e.g. persist/surface the floor and reasons), or treat it as someone else's problem?
